subject: Checkout latency and timeouts — coordination and short-term mitigations
messages:
From: Elena Soto <elena@sellsnap.com>
To: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops@sellsnap.com
Date: Wed, 10 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Checkout latency spikes — checkout timeouts and customer-impacting errors

Hi David,

We started seeing a sharp jump in checkout-side latency at ~08:55 PT — p95 for our /generate/checkout route climbed from ~480ms to ~1.8s and we've observed two client timeouts in the last 20 minutes. The failures are correlated with larger batched requests (payloads contain 5–10 items). We've attached a short log snippet and a perf trace.

Impact: checkout page retries and a small but visible conversion drop for two merchants (IDs attached). This is customer-facing and happening now.

Can you either: (a) confirm if this is a known rollout/traffic shift, or (b) get us a mitigation plan and ETA? We're happy to join a bridge — ops@sellsnap.com is ready.

Attachments: latency-snippet-20270310.txt (attached), perf-trace-08-55.json (attached)

Thanks,
Elena
Elena Soto
Head of Platform
SnapSell

Subject: Re: Checkout latency spikes — checkout timeouts and customer-impacting errors

Thanks for the heads up and the logs, Elena.

On Wed, Mar 10, 2027 at 09:12 AM Elena Soto <elena@sellsnap.com> wrote:
> We started seeing a sharp jump in checkout-side latency at ~08:55 PT...

We're standing up a short triage: Ben (SRE) — can you take initial telemetry and confirm whether this is runtime-side (KV/cache, batching) or model-side (kernel saturation)? Marissa (product) and Karthik (runtime) are on copy for tradeoffs.

Immediate plan (proposed):
- Start a 20-minute bridge to capture traces and coordinate mitigations.
- Roll a 10% canary to route a subset of checkout traffic to a dedicated pool (reduces noisy-neighbor risk).
- Temporarily increase KV cache TTL and reduce per-request KV warming to reduce overhead (only if SRE confirms safe).

Ben — please post a short summary and ETA in this thread; I will send Elena a customer-facing update within 30 minutes.

-David

David Kim
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Elena Soto <elena@sellsnap.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Mar 2027 09:33:30 -0700
Subject: Re: Checkout latency spikes — preliminary SRE triage

Quick triage notes from the first 10 minutes of telemetry:
- p95 for /generate/checkout: ~1.9s (baseline ~450ms). p99 ~4.8s.
- CPU/GPU saturation: a subset (~3/24) of nodes serving model v2.1.0 show GPU queue depth spikes during large batched requests.
- KV cache: sudden increase in cache miss rate and concurrent KV warm operations at the time of the spike. KV eviction rate up ~3x.

Immediate mitigations (low-risk):
1) Increase KV TTL from 30m -> 2h (reduces repeated warms). Rolling now to 10% of clusters, will expand if stable.
2) Reduce per-request KV warming concurrency (config flag warm.concurrency=2 -> 1) — small risk of cold responses on very rare queries, low downstream impact.
3) Route 10% -> 20% of checkout traffic to the dedicated pool (policy change) as a canary to test isolation.

I've opened ticket SRE-1945 with the traces and log snippets: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/SRE-1945
Attachments: kv-eviction-sample.png (attached), quick-heap-log.txt (attached)

ETA: TTL rollout andConcurrency change in ~12 minutes; routing canary should be active in ~18 minutes. Monitoring dashboard updated.

Ben
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Elena Soto <elena@sellsnap.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Mar 2027 09:44:10 -0700
Subject: Re: Checkout latency spikes — product tradeoffs and canary ask

Thanks Ben — helpful summary. A couple quick product-side questions before we flip routing at 20%:

1) Quality / functional impact: if we route to the dedicated pool (different infra + potentially different quantization profile), do we expect any change in generation fidelity that could affect checkout scoring or the business logic SnapSell runs? If so, we should surface that to Elena.

2) Canary sizing: David, can we start at 10% for 20 minutes and escalate to 20% if green? I prefer the smaller initial blast to reduce potential regressions.

3) KV warming disablement: Ben, how reversible is warm.concurrency=1 -> 2? What's the fallback plan if we see hallucination/timeout regressions?

Longer term: we should discuss a plan to harden batching for the checkout route (smarter batch slicing vs single large batches) and evaluate model q8_0 quantization on the dedicated pool. I'll file a product roadmap ticket after the bridge.

-marissa
Marissa Cole
Product Manager, Inference

Elena / SnapSell ops — quick update for your team:

- We've opened SRE-1945 and attached the traces/logs you sent to the ticket.
- Immediate mitigations applied: KV TTL increase rolling to 10% of clusters, per-request KV warming concurrency reduced to 1 (rolling).
- Starting a 10% canary to route checkout traffic to a dedicated pool now; we will hold at 10% for 20 minutes and expand to 20% if metrics look stable.
- Monitoring: p95/p99 dashboards and error rate are being tracked; I will update you at +30 and then after the 20-minute canary.

Proposed bridge: 10:30 PT for a 30-minute quick sync (we'll cancel if things stabilize sooner). Let me know if that works.

Links: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/SRE-1945 (ticket)

Thanks for the quick report and patience — we'll keep this tight.

-David
